statement: A scatterplot shows the age $x$, in years, and the resale value $y$, in dollars, of several used laptops of the same model. A line of fit for the data passes through the points $(2, 1550)$ and $(10, 350)$. According to this line of fit, what is the predicted resale value, in dollars, of a $7$-year-old laptop of this model?

choices.misconception: I averaged the two values, 1550 and 350, as if 7 years were halfway between 2 and 10 years.
I found the drop of 150 dollars per year but subtracted it for only 3 years, counting from 7 to 10, while starting from the value at 2 years.
I found 150 dollars per year but added 5 years of it to 1550, as if the value went up with age.

hints: Find the slope of the line through the two points.
The slope is $\dfrac{350 - 1550}{10 - 2}$ dollars per year. Then move from $x = 2$ to $x = 7$.
The slope is $-150$, and $7$ is $5$ years after $2$, so compute $1550 - 5 \cdot 150$.

solutions.reliable: The slope is $\dfrac{350 - 1550}{10 - 2} = \dfrac{-1200}{8} = -150$ dollars per year. From $(2, 1550)$, moving $5$ years to $x = 7$ changes the value by $5 \cdot (-150) = -750$, so the predicted value is $1550 - 750 = \$800$.
solutions.elegant: Check from the other point: going back $3$ years from $(10, 350)$ adds $3 \cdot 150 = 450$, giving $350 + 450 = 800$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
